title.narrative: Mozambique - Demonstrating C3 Living Units in Maputu and Beira to help rebuild Mozambique

description.narrative: In Mozambique there is an estimated housing shortage of 2 million and approximately 13.5 million people are living in unsuitable living conditions. The recent cyclone that hit the country ruined over 240.000 houses and the total damages for housing is estimated to be over 678 million US dollar. Under the brand of C3Living, Rendiz develops affordable flexible, transportable and sustainable living units using the cradle2cradle principle. The housing units may provide a solution to the affordable housing issues in Mozambique, including for low income households seeking to rebuild after the cyclone. In the Netherlands C3 Living is the cheapest solution in its kind and the company is now looking to expand its activities to Mozambique with the ambition to locally produce and market a minimum of 500 housing units yearly within 3 years. Demonstrating and testing the local adaptability of the units, as well as assessing the feasibility of locally producing them is required prior to further investment. Technical Assistance (DGGF) provided support for the selection of local partners, to develop a demonstration unit that meets local requirements, to map the potential supply chain, to assess the most efficient and cost-effective way to locally produce the units and support to develop a local end-user credit system (lease) for affordable housing. The project was successful and already supported 9 indirect jobs of locals who also received on the job training. Further investments in Mozambique are currently being explored to offer a solution to the urgent housing issues in the country. Each newly installed unit will support 5 direct jobs and further investments could lead to 2500 direct and indirect jobs.
